model.label: Tax-funded national health service: the state owns hospitals through four regional health authorities, municipalities run primary and long-term care, and the National Insurance Scheme (funded by payroll and personal contributions plus state transfers) pays GP fees and outpatient drugs, with nationally set co-payments under an annual ceiling

overview.statement: Responsibility is split across levels: the health ministry and its agencies handle planning, regulation and supervision; four regional health authorities manage specialist services and own the public hospitals, which are run as health trusts; and Norway's 357 municipalities organise primary care such as general practice, home care and nursing homes.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

overview.statement: Primary care is delivered mainly by self-employed GPs under contract with municipalities. Residents can pick a regular GP on a list system, and GPs act as gatekeepers to specialist care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

overview.statement: Coverage runs through the National Insurance Scheme (Folketrygden), administered by the Labour and Welfare Administration (NAV); every legal resident is enrolled automatically. Documented migrants get full access after six months of residence; for undocumented migrants, children are covered for basic services such as vaccinations and examinations, while adults are covered only for emergency acute care.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

overview.statement: The right of all residents to essential medical and care services, and the scope of coverage, are set in law: the Municipal Health and Care Act (2011), the Specialist Care Act (1999) and the National Insurance Act (1997).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

overview.statement: Compulsory health insurance began in 1909 for employees and their families, covering both care and income during illness; it was compulsory for low-income employees and optional for others. In 1956 it became a universal, mandatory right for all citizens (Commonwealth Fund).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Health care is financed mostly from general taxation, with National Insurance contributions as a complement (2025 Country Health Profile).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: The 2020 health system review put public sources at about 85% of health spending, of which about 74% came as transfers from general government (national, county and municipal tax revenue) and 11% from the National Insurance Scheme.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: National taxes pay for specialist (secondary) care and part of primary care; municipal taxes are the main funding source for primary care (2020 review).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: According to the 2020 review, the National Insurance Scheme's revenue came 32% from members' insurance contributions, 40% from payroll taxes and 28% from national taxes.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: The National Insurance Scheme is not only a health fund: it also pays income-related benefits such as retirement, survivor and disability pensions, and cash benefits for sickness, maternity, adoption and unemployment (2020 review).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Individual National Insurance contributions (trygdeavgift) in 2026 are 7.6% of wage income for people aged 17-69, 10.8% of self-employment income outside fishing, hunting and childminding (which pay 7.6%), and 5.1% of pension income and of the wage and business income of people under 17 or over 69. The lower income limit for calculating the contribution is NOK 99,650, and the contribution can never exceed 25% of personal income above that limit (Tax Administration).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Employers pay a payroll contribution to the National Insurance Scheme (arbeidsgiveravgift) that varies by region: across seven zones the 2026 rate falls from 14.1% in zone I to 0% in zone V, with lower rates in rural districts (Tax Administration).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: In 2018 the National Insurance Scheme made up 35% of the national budget (NOK 470 billion); members and employers paid for 67% of it and the state and other sources for the remaining third. (Commonwealth Fund).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: The Ministry of Health and Care Services divides the health budget among municipalities, counties, regional health authorities and the National Insurance Scheme through a distribution formula (the General Purpose Grant Scheme) that adjusts for differences in structural costs and tax revenue.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Public sources paid nearly 86% of current health spending in 2023, against an EU average of 80%; out-of-pocket payments made up 14%, against 16% in the EU (2025 Country Health Profile).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Voluntary health insurance accounted for only 0.2% of total health spending in 2023.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: Under the Tax Administration's 2024 guidance, an employer who pays an employee's treatment costs, or treatment (health) insurance, is as a starting point treated as paying taxable wages.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financing.statement: The 2020 review describes the main sources of tax revenue as personal income tax and VAT, with direct taxes making up about 70% of total tax revenue.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: There is no positive list of covered services; in practice public coverage includes approved prescription drugs on the 'blue list', prevention (check-ups, screening, childhood immunisation), primary care including GPs, physiotherapists and chiropractors, most specialist and hospital care, emergency care, nursing care, dental care for children and some other groups, and medical eye care, with glasses usually excluded (2020 review).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Non-medical eye care, most dental care for adults and complementary medicine are not paid for from public sources (2020 review).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Public coverage of inpatient care was nearly complete in 2022, and public sources covered 86% of outpatient care costs.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Only 27% of dental care costs were publicly funded in 2022, and public sources pay for about half of pharmaceutical spending.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Children under 18 get free public dental services while most adults pay the full cost; a 2025 amendment to the Dental Health Services Act extended coverage to people aged 19 to 28, who pay 25% of treatment costs with the public system covering 75%.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Who decides coverage: the scope of statutory coverage, the rules for co-payments and the safety net are set by parliament when it approves the annual public budget (2020 review).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: The 'New Methods' system decides on two levels: nationally, the regional health authorities decide jointly on the basis of assessments by the Medicines Agency and the Institute of Public Health; locally, hospitals decide on the basis of rapid assessments done in one hospital. The level depends on the technology, and medicines always go to the national level.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

covered.statement: Priority setting rests on three criteria: expected health benefit, the resources an intervention uses (fewer resources, higher priority), and the severity of the condition.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: Apart from hospital care, most publicly funded services carry nationally set co-payments, including consultations, treatments, follow-up visits and imaging.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: In 2026 the co-payment for an outpatient (polyclinic) visit is NOK 443 and for radiology, specialist ultrasound or nuclear-medicine imaging NOK 387; parliament sets the level in the state budget and the ministry fixes the amounts.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: The 2025 Country Health Profile gives the GP visit co-payment as NOK 155 (about EUR 15).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: The annual ceiling on approved co-payments is NOK 3,278 in 2026. Once a person has paid that much in a calendar year they receive an exemption card (frikort) and pay no approved co-payments for the rest of the year.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: Until 31 July 2026 children under 16 paid no co-payments; from 1 August 2026 this applies to everyone under 18.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: Since 1 January 2021 the two former co-payment ceilings (egenandelstak 1 and 2) have been combined into a single ceiling.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: Under the Blue Prescription Scheme, patients pay 50% of the cost, up to NOK 520 per prescription for a three-month supply, until the annual ceiling is reached; medicines outside the scheme, including non-prescription drugs, are paid for in full.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: People on the minimum state pension and patients with approved occupational injuries pay no user fees for blue-prescription medicines (Commonwealth Fund).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: In 2025 co-payments were removed for outpatient psychiatric care and substance-abuse treatment for young adults up to age 26.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

cost_sharing.statement: For long-term nursing home stays municipalities may charge an income-related fee of about 80% of the resident's after-tax income, capped at the actual cost; home nursing is free, while practical help at home can carry an income-related fee (Commonwealth Fund).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: A 2025 Consumer Council report found that loss of income and life crises such as separation, bereavement, serious illness or job loss are shared by many people who seek debt help, that some struggle with mental illness, and that debt and illness often form a vicious circle in which it is hard to tell which came first.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

financial_hardship.statement: Ukom, the Norwegian Healthcare Investigation Board, wrote in 2022 that collecting unpaid patient bills can come across as a faceless process, with claims passed automatically to debt collectors without the treating clinician knowing, and suggested it should be possible to reverse such collection claims.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Voluntary health insurance mostly gives supplementary cover: faster access to publicly covered non-emergency and outpatient care in semi-private or private facilities. Skipping waiting lists appears to be the main reason for buying it; about 10% of Norwegians (500,000) held a policy in 2016.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Companies are the main buyers: almost 90% of people with voluntary health insurance got it through their employer, and in 2016 group contracts outnumbered individual ones about ten to one (459,000 against 45,000).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: All voluntary health insurers are for-profit private companies; the four largest held 70% of the market in 2016.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: The Norwegian College of General Practice stated in 2024 that about 750,000 Norwegians have treatment insurance, almost 90% of it paid by employers.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

additional_care.statement: Buying treatment insurance requires a self-reported health declaration followed by a certificate from the GP; the College of General Practice says this lowers insurers' risk by screening buyers on their health at the time of purchase.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: In 2024 fewer than 2% of people who needed medical care reported an unmet need because of cost, distance or waiting time, about half the EU average; waiting times were the main reason given.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: People at risk of poverty were 2.5 times as likely as the general population to report unmet medical needs in 2024, a wider gap than the EU average ratio of 1.7.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: The mean wait for cataract surgery rose from 138 days in 2012 to 194 days in 2023 (up 41%), and for hip replacement from 154 to 192 days (up 25%).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: After the government's 2024 Waiting Time Promise, which raised hospital budgets substantially and backed digital and innovation measures, average waiting times fell through 2025 and were around 2019 levels by August-September 2025.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: At the end of 2023, 7 of 357 municipalities had no GP at all, and in Finnmark, Nordland and Møre og Romsdal counties GP shortages left 2-4% of residents without one.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

access.statement: Between 2012 and 2023 the yearly number of GP consultations per person increased from 3.1 to 3.6 among women and from 2.2 to 2.4 among men.

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)

outcomes.statement: Among patients aged 45 and over, 30-day mortality after a heart attack fell from 7.9% in 2013 to 5.9% in 2023, and after a stroke from 10.4% to 7.7%.

costs.statement: In 2023 Norway spent about EUR 5,672 per person on health (adjusted for purchasing power), the highest in Europe and nearly 1.5 times the EU average of EUR 3,832; as a share of GDP its spending (9.4%) was slightly below the EU average of 10.0%.

costs.statement: Only 3% of the health budget goes to prevention services (2022 data).

verification.checked_by: claude-opus-5-5 support review (passage vs. statement, separate cold pass, two rounds)
